clue.text: Position usually regarded as a temporary occupation

definitions.text: Position usually regarded as a temporary occupation

parts.words: Position usually regarded as a temporary occupation
parts.note: occupation read as job hides the sense of physically occupying a pitch for a few nights, as holidaymakers in tents do

explanation.surface: A job description for work that is only ever short-term.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitch for tents is a place people occupy only for a holiday's length, then leave.

clue.text: Sounds a prophet, but is rather a bore

indicators.note: the clue says the word for a prophet is how the answer is pronounced

parts.note: an augur foretold the future in ancient Rome

explanation.surface: Someone who sounds like a seer but is actually tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' looks like a dull person; it is a drill.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool for drilling holes in wood or earth, so a boring tool.

clue.text: A supporter of mine

parts.note: sounds like a fan of the speaker, but mine means a colliery, so a beam holding up a tunnel roof

explanation.surface: Someone describing a fan of theirs.
explanation.definitionFit: A timber post holding up the roof of a coal-working tunnel underground.

clue.text: Where little David returns in North America

indicators.note: the reversed name sits in between the two letters for North America
little David returns, so his short name is read backwards

parts.note: Dave is a short form of the name David

explanation.surface: Asking where a boy called David has come back to on the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns DAVE into EVAD, which goes 'in' NA.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state in the American West; the clue asks where, and the answer names a place.

clue.text: Having sampled army life I left and joined up

indicators.note: I left means the letter I departs from the word

parts.note: soldiered means served as a soldier

explanation.surface: A recruit who tried the army, quit, and then enlisted again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joined up' looks like enlisting but means fused with metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal pieces fused together with molten alloy are fixed, united.

clue.text: The embargoes on ancient capitalists

parts.note: embargoes are bans

explanation.surface: Trade embargoes imposed on old-time financiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capitalists' are not investors but residents of a capital city, ancient Thebes; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Citizens of Thebes, a capital city of ancient Greece and Egypt.

clue.text: An unforeseen down-to earth experience

parts.note: down-to-earth suggests something practical, but read literally it is an aircraft coming unexpectedly down to the ground

explanation.surface: A sudden practical, grounding moment in someone's life.
explanation.definitionFit: An emergency touchdown an aircraft is compelled to make, unplanned.

clue.text: No soft option for heroin ad diets

definitions.text: No soft option for heroin ad diets

parts.words: No soft option for heroin ad diets
parts.note: soft option suggests an easy choice, but soft and hard are the classes of narcotics, and heroin is one of the harder kind

explanation.surface: Getting off narcotics is no easy way out.
explanation.definitionFit: A strongly addictive narcotic, such as cocaine, unlike cannabis classed as soft.

clue.text: Revolutionary I'd call round to cover a popular story

parts.note: a red is a revolutionary, a communist

indicators.note: call goes round I'd, so the word for call contains it

parts.note: to ring is to call on the phone
taken as written, without the apostrophe
a hood is a head covering

explanation.surface: A radical phoning someone to cover for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' signals the container: the word for call wraps the I'd, rather than meaning a round of drinks; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known fairy tale about a girl, a wolf and her grandmother.

clue.text: Tough alternative or should be

indicators.note: an alternative form of the word Tough means its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hard choice, or what one is obliged to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternative' signals rearranging TOUGH; 'or' and 'be' are link words around the definition 'should'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are modal verbs of obligation: you ought to go means you should go.

clue.text: Look the other way across the Channel

definitions.text: Look the other way across the Channel

parts.words: Look the other way across the Channel
parts.note: a French phrase (from across the Channel) for turning round to face the opposite way, figuratively a reversal of opinion

explanation.surface: Advice to ignore what is happening in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look the other way' suggests ignoring something; here it is literal turning about, and 'across the Channel' says the term is French.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived term means an about-turn, a complete reversal of stance.

clue.text: Likely to be explosive in this case

definitions.text: Likely to be explosive in this case

parts.words: Likely to be explosive in this case
parts.note: case read as a matter or situation hides the literal casing that holds a gun's charge of powder

explanation.surface: A warning that a particular situation could blow up.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun round is a casing holding the propellant charge and bullet, so its contents explode.

clue.text: Summer danger

definitions.meaning: one who sums or totals figures
a venomous snake, a hazard to walkers

explanation.surface: Hazards of the hot season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summer' is the season on the surface but means someone who adds up.
explanation.definitionFit: One who tots up sums, and Britain's only venomous snake, a peril in the grass.

clue.text: Poorly piped note making for port

indicators.note: done poorly, the letters of piped come out jumbled

parts.note: E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone playing a pipe badly on the way to a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poorly' rearranges PIPED to DIEPP; add the note E. 'making for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Channel ferry harbour town in Normandy, France.

clue.text: Willing to finish in debt

parts.note: the end is the finish
owing means in debt

explanation.surface: Someone happy to end up owing money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Willing' looks like eager; it means leaving by a will.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean bequeathing, giving property or funds to someone by legacy.

clue.text: Gauged to make a Muse blush

indicators.note: the letters of a Muse are used to make something new, so they are rearranged

parts.note: to blush is to go red

explanation.surface: Something judged carefully enough to embarrass a goddess of the arts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' is the anagram signal on 'a Muse'; a Muse is one of the nine Greek goddesses of the arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean assessed by size or amount, as with a ruler or scale.

clue.text: Steps out with a lady of rank in Italy

parts.note: marches means walks out briskly

explanation.surface: A noblewoman striding out with someone in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian noblewoman, wife of a marquis.

clue.text: Something in the City with a family tree?

definitions.text: Something in the City with a family tree?

parts.words: Something in the City with a family tree?
parts.note: someone important in the City of London's government, read playfully as a tree (alder) plus a man

explanation.surface: Wondering about a City worker with a noble pedigree.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is the City of London, which elects senior civic officers to its Court; the question mark flags the split into a tree name and a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior elected civic councillor, a figure of note in local government such as the Corporation of London.

clue.text: It gives the others a right to try again

parts.note: the rest means the others

explanation.surface: A rule letting everyone else have another go.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean begin anew after stopping.

clue.text: A discarded garment worn in Spain

parts.note: a rag is a cast-off piece of clothing
clothes worn are on

explanation.surface: Someone in Spain wearing old cast-off clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'in Spain' points to a region found within Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A former kingdom, now an autonomous region, in north-east Spain.

clue.text: As Fleur might be moved to give tea to suitor

indicators.note: letters that might be moved can be shifted around into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl called Fleur being touched enough to serve a wooer tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might be moved' rearranges AS FLEUR. The definition is loose: the answer is what a rejected suitor gets, so 'tea' seems ironic.
explanation.definitionFit: A rejection, a turning down of an offer, such as a proposal of marriage.

clue.text: Notable Austrian from Harlem

indicators.note: made from the letters of the word, rearranged into a new one

explanation.surface: A famous Austrian who comes from New York's Harlem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' tells you to build the name out of the letters of HARLEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav, the late-Romantic composer and conductor born in Bohemia, Austrian Empire.

clue.text: Comes to mind at first light

definitions.meaning: becomes evident, as an idea that ... on someone
begins at daybreak, as a day does

explanation.surface: An idea occurring early in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to begin to be understood and for a day to break with sunrise.

clue.text: Banter doesn't get far with this bird

parts.note: chaff is light-hearted teasing
to inch is to move only slightly

explanation.surface: Teasing chatter that fails to make headway with a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A common European finch with a pink breast, a garden songbird.

clue.text: One is disturbed by it

indicators.note: letters disturbed are put out of order

explanation.surface: A complaint that a racket disturbs people.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines, and also rearranges ONE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwanted sound, which disturbs a person trying to rest.

clue.text: Matchless type

definitions.meaning: an old printers' size of type, six point

explanation.surface: Someone unrivalled in their kind.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means peerless, and printers also used it for a small six-point typeface.

clue.text: Grand soil ploughed up in Eire

indicators.note: soil ploughed up is turned over and broken, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Good earth turned over by a farmer in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ploughed up' rearranges G and SOIL; the definition 'in Eire' points to a place in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A county and town on the north-west coast of the Irish Republic.

clue.text: A crushing force on the way

definitions.text: A crushing force on the way

parts.words: A crushing force on the way
parts.note: sounds like an overwhelming power approaching, but literally a heavy road machine flattening the road surface

explanation.surface: A warning that an overwhelming power is coming.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy road-building vehicle with huge rollers that flattens tarmac; figuratively, an unstoppable force.
